extracted.intended_audience: HHS/FDA/DEA policymakers and small business stakeholders (medical device, dietary supplement, tobacco/premium cigar, herbal products, nursing advocacy)
extracted.subtask_description: Public-comment advocacy document (SBA Office of Advocacy) recommending deregulatory actions and specific revisions to numerous FDA/DEA guidances, rules, and agency practices to reduce burdens on small entities across medical devices, nursing, premium cigars, dietary supplements, and herbal products.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21 CFR Part 11 (electronic records) is outdated and unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations set forth the criteria under which the FDA considers electronic records to 'be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper.' Since the regulations were promulgated, the common use of electronic systems has greatly expanded. However, nearly 22 years later, Part 11 remains part of the CFR even though it is outdated and unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders suggest the FDA rescind Part 11 because it no longer reflects current electronic-record practices and imposes unnecessary burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 510(k) 'Best Practices for Selecting a Predicate Device' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Practices for Selecting a Predicate Device to Support a Premarket Notification 510(k) draft guidance recommends manufacturers select a predicate device that meets certain characteristics to support a 510(k) submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no statutory basis to make or enforce such recommendations. The draft also recommends disclosure regarding predicate device selection in a public-facing 510(k) summary, which is not a required element per 21 CFR § 807.92 and may inadvertently result in disclosure of proprietary information; the disclosure is irrelevant to substantial equivalence determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Evidentiary Expectations for 510(k) Implant Devices' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Evidentiary Expectations for 510(k) Implant Devices draft guidance appears to change the definition of an implanted medical device and includes blanket recommendations that do not consider device risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is inconsistent with the FDA’s longstanding benefit-risk and 'least burdensome' principles and may improperly expand regulatory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Use of Clinical Data in 510(k) Submissions' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Use of Clinical Data in Premarket Notification 510(k) Submissions draft guidance includes examples and recommendations related to the use of clinical data in 510(k) submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance suggests a deviation from the FDA’s statutory standard for substantial equivalence toward a PMA-level safety-and-effectiveness standard, imposing an undue burden; it should be eliminated or revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Evaluation of Thermal Effects of Medical Devices that Produce Tissue Heating and/or Cooling' draft guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft guidance on evaluation of thermal effects applies broadly across many device types and includes all premarket submissions, including IDE applications, without delineation across product lifecycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance is overly broad, inconsistent with IDE criteria, contrary to the 'least burdensome' approach directed by Congress, conflicts with FDA policies and recognized standards, lacks a risk-based approach, and will impede device development; stakeholders recommend withdrawal and collaborative development of tailored, standards-based policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit 506J guidance to statutory reporting only; narrow 506J Device List and 'additional notifications'
rubrics_metrics.description: Final guidance 'Notifying FDA of a Permanent Discontinuance or Interruption in Manufacturing of a Device Under Section 506J' updated prior guidance and included a 506J Device List and 'additional notifications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend withdrawing guidance that expands reporting beyond Section 506J statutory criteria. The FDA should focus solely on statutory reporting, narrow the Device List to items critical in a PHE consistent with Section 506J, increase transparency around shortage determinations and listing/delisting, and avoid imposing expansive 'additional notifications' that would strain supply chains and divert resources during PHEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Infusion Pumps Total Product Life Cycle' guidance's SAC expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2014 Infusion Pumps TPLC guidance introduced an expectation that a Safety Assurance Case (SAC) be submitted with all infusion pump 510(k) submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SAC framework, as implemented, does not improve safety and instead slows submissions and review of innovative devices; the SAC expectation should be withdrawn or revised to avoid unnecessary burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind outdated FDA cybersecurity guidance documents (2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cybersecurity for Networked Medical Devices Containing Off-the-Shelf (OTS) Software and related 2005 documents are outdated given the evolution of the cybersecurity landscape and newer statutory/regulatory expectations (e.g., §524B) and more comprehensive pre- and post-market guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents contain terminology no longer aligned with current guidance and have largely been superseded; rescission will reduce confusion and ensure stakeholders rely on up-to-date cybersecurity expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind draft LASIK patient labeling recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The LASIK Lasers – Patient Labeling Recommendations draft guidance proposes patient labeling approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders find the draft interferes with the patient-physician relationship, is not balanced, and fails to include both benefits and risks; FDA should rescind and collaborate with stakeholders for appropriate labeling recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind guidance documents superseded by later FDA recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain guidance documents (e.g., Hydrogen Peroxide-Based Contact Lens Care Products: Consumer Labeling Recommendations – Premarket Notification (510(k)) Submissions; User Labeling for Devices that Contain Natural Rubber) have been superseded by more recent FDA recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend rescinding these older documents to avoid redundancy and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Content and Format of Premarket Notification [510(k)] Submissions for Sharps Containers' guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on 510(k) content and format for sharps containers (1993) contains outdated recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent ISO standards (ISO 23907-1 and -2), recognized by FDA, cover many of the same safety and performance requirements; the guidance should be rescinded as obsolete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind 'Commercially Distributed Analyte Specific Reagents (ASRs)' FAQs guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The ASR FAQs interpret which products qualify as ASRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance interprets products more narrowly than the regulatory definition at 21 CFR 864.4020(a); FDA should rescind it to avoid inconsistent interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind Oncology Drug Products with Certain IVDs pilot guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance establishing a pilot program for oncology drug products used with certain IVD tests was issued without opportunity to comment and has seen no enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the pilot lacked prior comment, captured no participants, and may not be needed, the guidance should be rescinded if FDA continues the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defer to AATB standards for reducing MTBC and sepsis transmission in HCT/Ps; exempt processed tissues
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA issued guidance on reducing MTBC transmission and transmission of disease agents associated with sepsis for HCT/Ps; AATB issued new standards effective Jan 31, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA should defer to AATB standards 'solving' underlying risks. The FDA guidance, if implemented, would reduce supply of human tissue for implant substantially (~38%). At minimum, exempt tissues processed to remove viable cells because those processes eliminate virtually any MTBC transmission risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind/revise Pulse Oximeters guidance that diverges from ISO and imposes prescriptive clinical study requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA guidance on pulse oximeters diverges from draft ISO 80601-2-61, adds significant regulatory burden, and contains prescriptive recommendations for clinical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance appears to establish performance standards via guidance and requests new clinical data even when 510(k) submission is not required by 21 CFR 807.81(a)(3). Stakeholders recommend rescission or revision to align with consensus standards and avoid unnecessary burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind Recall Communications Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: CDRH Recall Communications Pilot communicates corrective actions that could lead to a recall prior to evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premature communication of corrective actions may cause unintended consequences. Statutory/regulatory mechanisms for corrective actions and recalls already exist (21 CFR Part 820.100; Part 806.10; Part 7) with timing requirements (e.g., reporting within 10 working days). The pilot duplicates/contradicts existing regime and should be rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update eSTAR v5.1 to remove enhanced Technical Screening text
rubrics_metrics.description: eSTAR is an interactive PDF that guides applicants through medical device submissions. FDA updated eSTAR and expanded Technical Screening language to make it more like a Refuse-to-Accept process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enhanced Technical Screening text is inconsistent with governing guidance and was uploaded without announcement; the enhanced text should be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise DEA special registration telehealth proposed rule: remove arbitrary 50% non-Schedule II prescription metric
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA proposed requiring at least 50 percent of prescriptions in a calendar month not be Schedule II narcotics as part of special registration for telehealth prescribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 50% threshold is unexplained and illogical; patient mixes vary monthly and this metric could unintentionally bar prescribers. The requirement should be removed or revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow telehealth prescribing across state lines when practitioner licensed in both states
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA proposed requiring patients and practitioners be physically located within the same state for telehealth prescribing of certain controlled substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates unnecessary barriers for patients who cross state lines for work/healthcare. HHS should work with DEA to explicitly allow cross-state telehealth prescribing provided the practitioner is licensed in both states where the practitioner and patient are physically located.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain telehealth waiver until revised DEA rule to avoid disruption of access
rubrics_metrics.description: Telehealth prescribers are operating under a waiver that allows patient access; DEA issued a proposed rule that may create new barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS/FDA should use influence to work with DEA and continue current waiver until a revised proposed rule is published to avoid harm to telehealth patients and prescribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude premium cigars from the Deeming rule
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA's Deeming rule concluded no justification to exempt premium cigars; stakeholders cite data showing premium cigars are a small percentage of market and consumed differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premium cigar stakeholders request exclusion from the Deeming rule based on consumption data (e.g., PATH, TTB) and published studies supporting differential use patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude premium cigars from the Very Low Nicotine rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In the proposed Very Low Nicotine rule, FDA acknowledged litigation regarding inclusion of premium cigars and indicated possible future actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the court ruling vacating inclusion of premium cigars and supporting evidence, stakeholders request premium cigars be excluded from the Very Low Nicotine rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude premium cigars from Tobacco Product Manufacturing Standards rule or redesign rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed Requirements for Tobacco Product Manufacturing Practice would impose broad compliance frameworks for all tobacco products, imposing significant costs on small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders assert the rule is fundamentally unsound for premium cigars, imposes enormous inappropriate costs with no public health benefit, and should be withdrawn or at least exempt premium cigars and be redesigned to agricultural rather than pharmaceutical product frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a specific federal definition of 'premium cigar' (8 elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders propose a federal definition consistent with court recognition: (1) wrapped in whole tobacco leaf; (2) contains 100% leaf tobacco binder; (3) contains ≥50% long filler tobacco by weight; (4) handmade/hand-rolled (no machinery beyond simple tools); (5) has no filter/nontobacco tip/mouthpiece; (6) no characterizing flavor other than tobacco; (7) contains only tobacco, water, vegetable gum with no other ingredients; (8) weighs more than 6 pounds per 1,000 units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt this definition to enable exclusions/exemptions and consistent regulatory treatment for premium cigars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt premium cigars from inappropriate FDA regulation to protect small businesses and stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders request exemptions and protections to avoid regulatory costs that serve no meaningful public health purpose and to ensure long-term stability for manufacturers, importers, retailers, and consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should protect small businesses from unnecessary regulatory costs and preserve market stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop consistent cigar categories and definitions for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies and regulatory actions suffer from inconsistent cigar categories/definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA, in consultation with federal agencies, should develop formal categories and definitions for cigars to ensure consistency among studies and regulatory analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove 'written assurances' requirements except where statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: FSMA-implementing regulations include 'written assurance' requirements for sellers and buyers to obtain annual/biannual written assurances from customers/vendors; these impose large costs and redundancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assurance requirements are burdensome (millions of documents) and often impossible for small entities with multilayered supply chains; FDA should rescind written assurance requirements except where required by law and apply enforcement discretion (FDA has announced open-ended enforcement discretion previously).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require FDA inspectors to cite specific regulations on Form 483
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA policy currently instructs inspectors not to quote regulations when reporting observations on Form 483, leaving recipients unclear which regulatory element is implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To improve transparency and facilitate rapid compliance—particularly for small businesses—FDA should revise the Inspections Operations Manual to require investigators include references to underlying cGMP (and other) regulations for each relevant Form 483 observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply enforcement discretion/exemptions for very small establishments under 21 CFR Part 111
rubrics_metrics.description: 21 CFR Part 111 (dietary supplement cGMP) imposes compliance costs that are especially burdensome for very small establishments; original FDA estimates likely understated burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA should apply formal enforcement discretion for very small firms (proposed: < $250,000 annual sales, 3-year rolling average, inflation-adjusted) provided they (a) comply with local health regs, (b) for processed-ingredient purchases obtain and review vendor COAs, and (c) do not use botanical ingredients listed Safety Class 2a or 3 in the AHPA Botanical Safety Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow master manufacturing records (MMR) to cover a range of batch sizes under conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Current 21 CFR § 111.205(a) requires an MMR for each unique formulation and for each batch size, which is burdensome and sometimes unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend § 111.205(a) to permit an MMR to cover a range of lot or batch sizes so long as (a) relative proportions of all components, (b) equipment, (c) in-process specifications, and (d) packaging components remain the same for sizes within the range, and each batch record created from the MMR is reviewed and approved by quality control prior to use. Alternatively allow MMRs to cover a range where lot size is fixed but number of lots per batch varies. For packaging, no separate MMR for each batch size if process parameters do not vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow supplement manufacturers to operate with only one employee (revise § 111.210(h)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Current cGMP language indirectly requires two people for certain manual operations (weighing, addition, verification), effectively precluding one-employee firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is unnecessarily prescriptive and ignores automation; it imposes significant cost on one-person firms. Recommend replacing § 111.210(h)(3)(ii) with wording consistent with infant formula cGMP rules accommodating single-employee operations while ensuring adequate controls (the comment provides proposed replacement language).
